evidence.note: Deliberately installs the real Stripe SDK 'for testing' and runs an end-to-end smoke test through it against the service — verifying via the same SDK the verifier uses, well beyond curl happy-paths.

Inspects the idempotency error-response shape and how the SDK maps error type to exception (IdempotencyError class, base error init) — targeted compatibility checks on the cached-error-body / envelope trap, not just 200s.
Writes a second 'hard cases' smoke test (smoke2.py), then restarts the server and re-runs both hard and base smokes after changes — regression-style re-verification.
Verifies module imports, boots server, hits health and creates a customer — baseline smoke coverage of CRUD/health before deeper checks.

reasoning: The agent verifies through the actual `stripe` SDK against the service and builds targeted checks for the idempotency/error-envelope trap (inspecting cached error-body shape and SDK exception mapping) plus a dedicated 'hard cases' test rerun after fixes — clearly above the boot-and-smoke level of anchor 5. However, there is no visible verification of the deeper temporal/concurrency traps (webhook 5xx retry/backoff, serialized same-key retries) nor of pagination and restricted-key 403s that anchor 8/10 require, so it sits at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
